style: A classic Korean folktale told on a cold mountain-village night. Intimate cinematic delivery with humane, dry comedy and a mounting rhythm of mistaken fear. Never sound childish, broad, theatrical, or commercial. Leave a short natural breath after every line. Pronounce gotgam as got-gahm, the Korean word for dried persimmon.

speakers.name: Narrator
speakers.style: A warm mature storyteller, observant and unhurried, with understated amusement rather than a performed moral.

speakers.name: Mother
speakers.style: A tired but affectionate mother soothing a baby at night; soft, practical, and never alarmed.

speakers.name: Cattle thief
speakers.style: A cautious young man whispering to himself in the dark, pleased with what he thinks is a lucky find.

speakers.name: Tiger
speakers.style: A large proud tiger whose deep voice suddenly cracks with sincere, urgent fear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: On a cold night, a hungry tiger came down from the mountain and slipped into a village.
lines.direction: Open quietly and visually; give cold night and hungry tiger weight without menace.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beneath one roof, he heard a baby crying and crept closer to the warm paper window.
lines.direction: Draw the listener from the wide mountain into the warm, intimate window; lightly quicken on crept closer.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.text: Hush now. A tiger will hear you and come.
lines.direction: Low and soothing, an ordinary bedtime warning; no fear or melodrama.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The baby cried even louder. The tiger blinked. Was this tiny child truly not afraid of him?
lines.direction: Land the first two sentences dryly, then let the final question carry the tiger's wounded disbelief.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.direction: Gentle and matter-of-fact, as if offering a familiar small treat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The crying stopped at once. The tiger trembled. This thing called gotgam must be more terrible than a tiger!
lines.direction: Begin with crisp surprise; expand the final sentence into sincere comic awe, never a shout.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That same night, a cattle thief slipped into the shed, feeling through the darkness for the strongest cow.
lines.direction: Reset into furtive quiet and make the darkness spatial; retain a trace of knowing amusement.

lines.speaker: Cattle thief
lines.text: This one! A little too hairy... but strong.
lines.direction: Whispered satisfaction, then puzzled hesitation at hairy, finishing with self-reassurance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He climbed onto the tiger. One thought he had found a cow; the other thought gotgam had caught him.
lines.direction: Clear and balanced; treat the two mistaken thoughts as a matched comic pair.

lines.speaker: Tiger
lines.direction: Deep but suddenly terrified, urgent and breathless; run is a private command to himself.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The tiger raced into the forest while the thief clung tight—one afraid of the thing above, the other of the tiger below.
lines.direction: Fast, clean chase rhythm; slow just enough after the dash for the mirrored fear to register.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At dawn, the thief saw stripes and leapt into a pine. The tiger fled the other way. Neither looked back. The dried persimmon was still only the baby’s supper.
lines.direction: Resolve swiftly, then soften and slow the final sentence with warm, dry clarity; do not preach.
